title: Faith as a dark light (Ascent 2)
hook: faith guides like a light we can't look at directly

segments.voice: Yesterday, remora: a thin thread holds as well as a cord. Your line was a thread still holds. Which thread did you cut? Today, how John says we find our way in the dark. Day two hundred sixty-six.

Driving a country road at night, you never see your own headlights. You see by them: the white line, the edge of the ditch, a deer by the fence, a few yards of road at a time. Beyond that, black. You couldn't describe the light itself, and yet everything you see out there comes through it. John of the Cross says faith works something like that. It's a light. But from the inside, it feels like darkness. Today's word is that strange light.
screen: `A COUNTRY ROAD AT NIGHT.` → `YOU SEE BY THE HEADLIGHTS.` → `A LIGHT THAT FEELS LIKE DARK.`

segments.voice: First, a dark night. In the second book of the Ascent, John calls faith itself a dark night for the soul. Faith, he says, asks us to trust what we can't see, touch or prove, on the word of God. That's dark to the mind, which wants to see for itself. But he adds: the darker it is for the mind, the more light it gives the soul. Second, the cloud. John points to the Exodus story. As Israel escapes Egypt, a pillar of cloud stands between them and the army chasing them. The Douay-Rheims says: "it was a dark cloud, and enlightening the night." Dark on one side, light on the other. The same cloud. John says that's faith: darkness to our understanding, light for our way. Third, the walk. Saint Paul says, in the Douay-Rheims: "For we walk by faith, and not by sight." Walking isn't the same as understanding. You can walk a path you can't see the end of, one step, in trust. Fourth, why not visions? John warns people not to chase visions, voices and special signs. They can be misleading, he says, and even true ones can become something to cling to. Faith is the surer guide, precisely because it's plain, humble and dark. Look back at this week. One dark night, and a house at rest. Sweetness: dry is not gone. Three signs: the longing stays. Isaiah: bigger than your idea. Nada: nothing, then everything. A bird on a thread. And today, a light we can't look at but see by. It's all one night.
screen: `FAITH IS DARK TO THE MIND.` · `A DARK CLOUD THAT LIGHTS THE NIGHT.` · `WALKING, NOT SEEING.` · `DON'T CHASE VISIONS.` · then, large: `FOR WE WALK BY FAITH, AND NOT BY SIGHT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: trust one thing you can't see. Settle and breathe. Think of something in your life that's unresolved, where you can't see the end. A diagnosis, a job, a child's choices, a question about God. Don't try to solve it. Picture it as a path in the dark, and yourself taking just one step. If you pray, you can hand the unseen part to God and ask only for the next step. If you don't, name the one step you can see. The bell holds the time.
Dark cloud. The image from Exodus John uses for faith in the Ascent: dark to our understanding on one side, yet lighting our way on the other. Today's word.
Your line: walk by faith. Today, take the one step you can see, and leave the rest of the path for later. Day two hundred sixty-six.

howItsDone: Catholics describe faith as trust in what God has revealed rather than in what they can see or prove, and spiritual directors in the Carmelite tradition steer people away from seeking visions toward plain faith.
